scope: Ten remaining exact-v1 standard routes; claims are restricted to the disclosed workload, evaluator and implementation boundary.

reviews.claim: Audio-video synchronization quality needs a reference-free continuous score over causal-semantic alignment, not only temporal-offset metrics or discrete language verdicts.
reviews.mechanism: SynthSync pairs generated audio with real videos and human preferences; an omni-modal backbone receives pairwise preference training, replaces its discrete head with a continuous projection and is post-trained with real-valued GRPO.
reviews.artifact_boundary: Human-preference correlation on SynthSync supports the metric claim; it does not make the learned evaluator a physical-synchrony oracle.
reviews.proved: The trained scorer ranks the disclosed generative failures closer to human preferences than named temporal and omni-LLM baselines.
reviews.not_proved: It does not establish evaluator robustness across generators, cultures, domains or adversarial optimization against the learned score.
reviews.trade_off: A learned continuous evaluator captures richer defects but creates benchmark, judge and reward-hacking dependence.

reviews.claim: Knowledge-graph fact verification benefits from separating query-rewrite competence from iterative retrieval-policy optimization.
reviews.mechanism: A first training stage stabilizes natural-language queries derived from triples; a second GRPO stage optimizes when and how to search, reconcile evidence and stop before producing the fact-verification label.
reviews.artifact_boundary: Evidence is limited to the stated T-REx seen/unseen splits, F1 and search-call count; industrial-KG reliability is an aspiration, not a demonstrated deployment.
reviews.proved: The two-stage model improves the reported verification F1 while reducing search calls relative to selected baselines.
reviews.not_proved: It does not establish open-web truth, calibrated confidence, robustness to poisoned evidence or transfer beyond the benchmark predicates.
reviews.trade_off: Specialized training controls retrieval cost but adds reward design, staged data and failure coupling between rewrite and search policies.

reviews.claim: A bug reproduction test is an intermediate executable evidence artifact, so coding agents need separate localization, path analysis, assertion planning, execution and repair stages.
reviews.mechanism: ReProAgent extracts issue evidence, narrows repository locations hierarchically, constructs and executes a reproduction test in Docker, and uses runtime feedback to refine it across several code-capable model backends.
reviews.artifact_boundary: The evaluation uses Python SWT-bench repositories and standardized containers; framework or model versions outside v1 are not assumed equivalent.
reviews.proved: On the reported issues, the staged workflow generates more executable reproduction tests than the named baselines across several backbones.
reviews.not_proved: It does not establish other languages, flaky/concurrent defects or that a passing reproduction test isolates the actual root cause.
reviews.trade_off: Executable evidence improves debuggability but costs sandbox execution and can overfit tests to symptoms rather than causes.

reviews.claim: Whole-arm manipulation needs a receding-horizon controller that represents contact explicitly and combines analytical kinematics with learned latent dynamics.
reviews.mechanism: TACTIC fuses RGB, depth, proximity, force and proprioception, predicts action-conditioned latent transitions, samples contact-aware joint velocities and executes through a compliant low-level controller before replanning.
reviews.artifact_boundary: Simulation and reported hardware trials evaluate task success and force behaviour; no formal safety guarantee is claimed.
reviews.proved: In the stated environments, contact-centric sensing, hybrid modeling and sampling improve success/safety metrics over the selected learned controls.
reviews.not_proved: Arbitrary planner outputs remain dependent on compliant hardware, watchdogs and emergency stops, and broad real-world robustness is open.
reviews.trade_off: Explicit contact state improves control but adds sensing, calibration, model-predictive compute and low-level safety dependencies.

reviews.claim: Long-context evaluation should vary natural evidence geometry and source scale, because token length alone does not reveal whether a system can preserve entity bindings and cross-passage relations.
reviews.mechanism: WildTrace curates naturally distributed evidence trails, labels forward, intersection, comparative, temporal and counterfactual geometry, and reports scale-tier curves plus source-cluster diagnostics.
reviews.artifact_boundary: Leaderboard scores are tied to the released question/document set and multi-judge matrix; diagnostic slices are not independent leaderboards.
reviews.proved: The evaluated systems show graded, geometry-dependent degradation rather than one universal context cliff.
reviews.not_proved: The benchmark does not isolate architectural causality or guarantee that its natural trails represent private enterprise corpora.
reviews.trade_off: Natural evidence improves ecological validity but reduces experimental control and complicates attribution across source families.

reviews.claim: Programs that are test-equivalent can differ substantially in deductive verifiability, so coding-agent diversity should vary implementation structure before verifier-guided repair.
reviews.mechanism: Diversify2Verify generates several WhyML implementation families from one accepted contract, type-checks and tests them, sends each to a prover and applies bounded repair to localized proof obligations.
reviews.artifact_boundary: Public LeetCode-derived tasks may be contaminated; the claim concerns generated WhyML structures and verifier outcomes, not unseen coding ability.
reviews.proved: In the benchmark, task-equivalent implementation families yield different proof success and many remaining failures are localized obligations after repair.
reviews.not_proved: Verification failure does not imply program incorrectness, and benchmark contracts may themselves be incomplete.
reviews.trade_off: Structural diversity increases proof reach but multiplies generation and verification cost and complicates selection among equivalent artifacts.

reviews.claim: Bug-report usefulness is determined by specific evidence fields and repository difficulty, not raw report length; issue text is the repair agent's task specification.
reviews.mechanism: The study combines observational reports with controlled deletion of expected behaviour, observed behaviour, reproduction steps and code pointers, then fits repository-aware mixed-effect success models across three LLMs.
reviews.artifact_boundary: Fields are coded largely as present/absent and deletions are artificial; odds ratios remain tied to the sampled repositories and agents.
reviews.proved: For the evaluated issues, information types have different associations and causal-ablation effects on repair success, while repository-level variance remains large.
reviews.not_proved: The study does not measure information quality continuously or establish a universal bug-report template.
reviews.trade_off: Structured issue evidence helps agents but increases reporter burden and can give false confidence when fields are present but wrong.

reviews.claim: Open-ended intelligence may require expanding the representation and verifier vocabulary, not only searching harder inside a fixed problem space.
reviews.mechanism: The position paper models progress as reducing discrepancy between current representational state and an incompletely specified goal, and identifies vocabulary and verifier gaps as barriers to concept and task invention.
reviews.artifact_boundary: This is a conceptual framework without a new empirical evaluation contract; it can motivate a structural question but cannot support implementation or performance claims.
reviews.proved: No empirical mechanism is proved; the paper provides terminology for a design pressure beyond fixed-state optimization.
reviews.not_proved: It does not show how to safely create new representations or validate novel verifier spaces.
reviews.trade_off: Expanding vocabularies may enable novelty while weakening comparability, formal guarantees and controllability.

reviews.claim: Agent release gates should classify autonomy, action/tool scope and impact, then trigger controls and reassessment when those properties change.
reviews.mechanism: ARC adapts NIST, ISO and regulatory risk concepts into an agent-specific rubric, assigns tiers from scored capabilities and supplies lifecycle reassessment triggers.
reviews.artifact_boundary: The rubric is an internally created framework, not an authoritative legal classification or validated predictor of harm.
reviews.proved: The paper demonstrates a structured mapping and case application, not reduction of real incidents.
reviews.not_proved: Subjective scoring, lifecycle drift and rapid capability change remain explicit limitations.
reviews.trade_off: Tiering makes controls reviewable but can collapse contextual risk into one score and become stale between reassessments.

reviews.claim: Multi-model task allocation needs calibrated competence and cost rather than self-reported confidence; an auction is useful only when bids are commensurable.
reviews.mechanism: Agora decomposes tasks, solicits calibrated model/tool bids, allocates subtasks under quality-first or cost-aware policies, executes in parallel where possible and aggregates results.
reviews.artifact_boundary: Results use the benchmark-specific model pools and calibration procedure in exact v1; provider prices, latency and availability are not universal.
reviews.proved: On the disclosed text, science-code and vision tasks, calibrated allocation improves several quality metrics over stated routing baselines; the no-calibration ablation degrades many tasks.
reviews.not_proved: It does not establish truthfulness of bids under strategic agents, production tail latency or optimal allocation under nonstationary backends.
reviews.trade_off: Auction allocation exposes cost-quality choices but adds calibration data, orchestration latency and correlated failure among bidders.
